source_snapshot: fetched 2026-08-01; NMW page states 'The rates change on 1 April every year', so this snapshot is the April 2026 set
_why_this_candidate: Top-ranked in the non-coding pack strategy: jurisdiction-specific bureaucracy. Statutory values are set by policy rather than derived, they change on a fixed annual date, they are consequential to get wrong (an employer underpaying wages is breaking the law), and they give free deterministic evals because the correct answer is a published number. The privacy story is also the strongest of any candidate — payroll and tenancy questions are exactly what people will not send to a hosted model — which makes a local model the only option and the pack existence rather than optimisation.
judge_or_compute: JUDGE, with one caveat worth stating. Every probe here is recall of a published value or a published rule: a rate, a deadline, a scheme name, an eligibility boundary. None requires the model to compute anything. The caveat is that DOWNSTREAM tasks in this domain — 'what redundancy pay is owed to this person' — are arithmetic over these values, and arithmetic is exactly what small models are unreliable at. So the packable half is the VALUES AND RULES; any calculator built on top is a tool, and the pack must not claim to do the sum.

probes.q: What is the UK National Living Wage hourly rate for someone aged 21 or over?
What is the UK National Minimum Wage hourly rate for an 18 to 20 year old?
What is the UK National Minimum Wage hourly rate for a worker under 18?
What is the UK apprentice minimum wage hourly rate?
On what date do UK National Minimum Wage rates change each year?
probes.span: The rates change on 1 April every year.

probes.q: A UK apprentice is 22 years old and in the second year of their apprenticeship. Which minimum wage rate applies to them?
probes.span: aged under 19, or aged 19 or over and in the first year of their apprenticeship, receive the apprentice rate

probes.q: What is the UK Statutory Sick Pay weekly rate?
probes.span: You can get up to £123.25 per week Statutory Sick Pay (SSP)

probes.q: For how many weeks can UK Statutory Sick Pay be paid?
probes.span: It's paid by your employer for up to 28 weeks.

probes.q: How long does a UK landlord have to put a tenancy deposit into a protection scheme?
probes.span: Your landlord or letting agent must put your deposit in the scheme within 30 days of getting it.

probes.q: Once a UK landlord and tenant agree how much of the deposit is returned, how long does the landlord have to return it?
probes.span: Your landlord must return your deposit within 10 days of you both agreeing how much you'll get back.

probes.q: Name the government-approved tenancy deposit protection schemes in England and Wales.
probes.span: Deposit Protection Service; MyDeposits (including deposits held by Capita); Tenancy Deposit Scheme
